subject: CloudCrest renewal — bakeoff findings and retention plan
messages:
From: Asha Patel <asha@cloudcrest.com>
To: stephanie_nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@cloudcrest.com
Date: 2026-10-24T09:03:00-07:00
Subject: Results from vendor bakeoff / next steps

Stephanie — thanks again for the Redwood team running the trial last week. We completed the internal bakeoff and I wanted to share the summary: competitor X delivered lower average p99 latency on long sequences, and our SREs flagged a few OOM-like dropouts during heavy burst testing. I've attached the raw logs and our latency CSV.

We still value Redwood's reliability and features (observability, rollout controls), but the cost delta + the p99 gap has our procurement team asking for a commercial/technical remediation plan before renewal. Can we get a proposed amendment (term + capacity) and a short remediation timeline by next Thursday 10/28? Procurement also requested an indicative committed capacity discount.

Thanks — happy to hop on a quick call if helpful.

— Asha
[Attachment: cloudcrest-bakeoff-logs.zip (zip)]

From: stephanie_nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
To: Asha Patel <asha@cloudcrest.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, nikhil_sharma <nikhil_sharma@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-24T11:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Results from vendor bakeoff / next steps

Asha — appreciate the clear summary and the logs. Sorry to hear about the p99 gap and the OOM signals. We're on it.

Internal plan: I'll loop in Marissa and Nikhil to propose a concrete remediation + amendment by 10/28. Short answers up front: yes we can provide a revised committed capacity discount and a temporary elevated support SLA to cover the next 90 days while you transition to the new configuration.

Would you be open to a 30-minute call on 10/26 to review the logs together and walk through our suggested kernel/quantization tweak + autoscale adjustments? If yes, share a preferred time.

— Stephanie
VP, Accounts — Redwood Inference

From: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Folks — passing this to sequence a save-plan. Quick notes:
- Deal tile: CLD-4821 (renewal Q4). Current ARR: $1.2M. Renewal window 11/15.
- External ask: remediation plan + committed capacity discount. Procurement wants numbers by 10/28.
- Risk: competitor X has lower p99 on long sequences; CloudCrest is price-sensitive and capacity-constrained.

Proposed split of work: Nikhil — lead the technical remediation doc and propose a target p99 profile + quick config we can push. Rishi — prepare a 90-day elevated support SOW and SLA uplift to reduce churn risk. Stephanie/Marissa — we own commercial amendment + pricing.

I'll schedule a run-through on 10/26 10:00am PT; Nikhil please prepare a side-by-side latency diff and recommended runtime knobs.

— Marissa
Account Executive

From: nikhil_sharma <nikhil_sharma@redwood.com>
To: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, stephanie_nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-25T08:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Results from vendor bakeoff / next steps

Adding my preliminary findings after a quick pass on the logs:
- The OOMs correlate with high-concurrency bursts where KV cache warming was disabled by their test harness. Enabling prefix caching & bumping the per-request KV window eliminates the majority of the spikes.
- Competitor X uses a trimmed attention kernel that helps at seq_len>4096; we can match p99 by switching to our alternate kernel + a mild per-token quantization (int8) for the heavy batch path. Expected accuracy hit <1.2% per our evals.
- Quick deliverables for 10/28: a technical remediation doc, a patch runtime config that we can stage into their Dedicated pool, and a suggested rollback plan.

I'll attach the latency comparison CSV and outline.

— Nikhil
Senior Solutions Engineer
[Attachment: latency-comparison-2026-10-22.csv]

From: stephanie_nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
To: Asha Patel <asha@cloudcrest.com>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, nikhil_sharma <nikhil_sharma@redwood.com>, rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-26T10:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Results from vendor bakeoff / next steps

Asha — thanks for taking the call this morning. Per the run-through and Nikhil's patch testing, here's what we can commit to by 11/05:

1) Technical remediation (no-op risk): deploy kernel + KV cache tweaks into a staged environment; expected p99 improvement ~18-22% on long sequences.
2) Commercial amendment: 12-month renewal with a tiered committed capacity discount (details below) and a one-time credit of $40k to offset migration costs.
3) Temporary SLA uplift: 30-day elevated SLO to 99.8% p99 availability with a named escalation engineer on-call for 90 days.

Draft amendment attached (proposed-amendment-CLD-4821.pdf). Marissa and I will propose the redlines in HubSpot; Rishi will own the SOW.

Next steps: please confirm whether procurement needs the DocuSign-ready amendment or a spreadsheet with cost math first. If DocuSign, we can get it to you by 11/02.

— Stephanie

From: Asha Patel <asha@cloudcrest.com>
To: stephanie_nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

- Procurement asked that the committed discount be a guaranteed rate for 24 months (they want price stability). Can you run the numbers for a 24-month commit and send a DocuSign amendment?
- Our CTO wants one more short stress test with the patched runtime on our staging cluster (we will schedule for next week). If that passes, procurement expects to sign the amendment.

We are close — procurement & engineering both signaled positive movement. Please send the 24-month numbers and the DocuSign link when ready.

— Asha
CloudCrest Procurement
